title: Candy
hints: the rule only ever compares a child to their immediate left and right neighbor - can you satisfy the 'left neighbor' half of the rule and the 'right neighbor' half of the rule in two separate, simpler passes?

left-to-right pass: if ratings[i] > ratings[i-1], this child must beat their left neighbor, so set candies[i] = candies[i-1] + 1 - this pass alone correctly satisfies every 'increasing from the left' requirement

right-to-left pass: if ratings[i] > ratings[i+1], this child must beat their right neighbor, so candies[i] needs to be at least candies[i+1] + 1 - but this child might already have a larger value from the left pass, so take the max rather than overwriting

after both passes, does taking candies[i] = max(leftPassResult[i], rightPassResult[i]) for every position guarantee both directions' constraints hold simultaneously? yes, because each pass only increases a value to satisfy its own direction, and taking the max preserves whichever pass's requirement was stricter at each position, without violating the other

why must both passes start every child at a baseline of 1 candy, and why is it safe to never decrease a value once set? because every child needs at least 1 candy regardless of ratings, and once a constraint is satisfied by a large enough value, only increasing further (never decreasing) can keep it satisfied while fixing new violations found later in the pass
commonMistakes: only doing a single left-to-right pass, which correctly handles rising sequences but fails on a rating that rises then falls (like [1,2,2,1] with a strict drop after a peak), since it never accounts for the right-neighbor requirement
in the right-to-left pass, unconditionally setting candies[i] = candies[i+1] + 1 instead of taking the max with the existing value, which can overwrite and violate the left-to-right pass's result
giving extra candies for ties (equal adjacent ratings), when the rule only requires strictly more candies for strictly higher ratings

content.problemStatement:
A teacher wants to give candies to children standing in a line, based on their ratings, given in the array `ratings`. Every child must get at least one candy.

**Any child with a strictly higher rating than an immediate neighbor must receive strictly more candies than that neighbor. Return the minimum total number of candies needed.**
notes: all ratings equal (every child gets exactly 1 candy)
strictly increasing ratings (candies must strictly increase left to right)
strictly decreasing ratings (candies must strictly decrease left to right)
a single peak in the middle with ratings rising then falling

sampleTestCases.explanation: give candies [2, 1, 2]: the first child beats their right neighbor's rating so needs more candies than them, and the third child beats their left neighbor's rating so also needs more, giving 2+1+2=5

give candies [1, 2, 1]: the second child has a strictly higher rating than the first so needs more candies, but the third child ties the second child's rating so no extra candy is required between them, giving 1+2+1=4

optimal.pattern: two left-to-right and right-to-left passes, each enforcing the rule against one neighbor direction, then take the elementwise max

bruteForce.approach: start everyone at 1 candy, then repeatedly scan all neighbor pairs and bump up any child that violates the higher-rating-more-candy rule, looping until a full pass makes no changes
bruteForce.time: O(n^2) in the worst case (a full pass may be needed for every position adjustment)
